frontier.hypothesis: One of the function's OWN constants can serve as a threshold-decay carrier, making the confirmed decay lever reachable from ordinary C: specifically, whether a named holder for the `0xA` ramp step is actually MOVED (lifetime >= 1) or folded to lifetime 0 by cse1.
frontier.mechanism: A movable is moved only if m->lifetime >= 1 (tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:791); lifetime is 0 when cse1 has folded the constant into a 16-bit-immediate insn and left the holder with no surviving use. `addiu` takes an immediate, so the prediction is life 0 - but 0xA occurs at six sites (case 1 twice, case 3 once, case 2 once, case 4 twice) and if even some of them survive as register-required uses the k >= 8 requirement is suddenly within reach of ordinary C.
frontier.next_probe: Declare a single `s32 step = 0xA;` at the top of the loop body, use it at all six sites, run dump.ps1 and read the func_8007526C section of tmp/grind/func_8007526C/dumps/text1b.loop for a movable on that regno and its `life N` field. Then repeat with six separate holders to see whether six decrements materialise. Read the dump BEFORE reading the score - the score will be worse either way; the `life` field is the answer.

frontier.hypothesis: The loop exit test can supply threshold-decay carrier #1 at zero or negative instruction cost by being spelled as an eq/ne comparison against a held constant instead of `i < 2`.
frontier.mechanism: The MIPS branch predicate is reg_or_0_operand, so `while (i != n)` with n = 2 forces the 2 into a register that cse1 cannot fold away - a movable with lifetime >= 1 that hoists to the pre-header and decrements threshold by 3 (loop.c:1904), while removing the in-loop `slti` the current form emits.
frontier.next_probe: Measure `i = 0; do { ... i++; } while (i != 2);` on the candidate chassis: read build_insns for the cost delta against 93 and the .loop dump for whether a new movable appears and is 'moved to' the pre-header. Note the target's own exit test is `slti $v0,$a2,0x2; bnez` (asm/funcs/func_8007526C.s:97-98), so this carrier trades two target-matching instructions for one decrement - bank the exact trade even if the net score rises.

frontier.hypothesis: s8's moved_once doubling remains the single cheapest confirmed route to the target's movable shape, and its only open problem is still an arming loop whose emitted control code is absorbed.
frontier.mechanism: move_movables' `if (moved_once[regno]) insn_count *= 2;` at tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c:1609-1611 permanently doubles the local insn_count for every movable scanned after the first already-moved one; moved_once is per-function (allocated loop.c:344, set loop.c:1912) and loop_optimize walks loop numbers downward, so a nested or textually-later loop is processed first and arms it.
frontier.next_probe: Two arming routes are now closed - do-while(0) is rejected as phony at loop.c:570 (s8) and same-value matching never sets moved_once (this session, loop.c:1912/:1968). What remains untested is an arming loop placed textually AFTER the main loop whose induction variable and body are work the function already performs, and the `while (i < 2) { do { ...; i++; } while (i < 2); }` same-back-edge shape, which requirement (c) predicts will fail because the inner loop contains the dispatch - measure it once purely to confirm that prediction cheaply.
